title: Network Troubleshooting
summary: Use synthetic link, interface, address, gateway, DNS, and latency evidence to reason about connectivity.
objectives: Use multiple clues to narrow a simulated network problem.
Explain why a diagnostic command must target an approved sandbox host.

vocab.def: A system that connects a local network to another network.
A service that helps translate names into network addresses.
The time it takes information to travel between points.

sections.heading: A connection has layers
sections.body: A simulated problem may involve the physical link, interface status, IP configuration, gateway, DNS, switch path, or service. Check evidence in a deliberate order.

sections.heading: Compare clues
sections.body: If an interface is down, a higher-level name lookup cannot fix it. If a name resolves but the service is slow, latency or the service may need investigation.

sections.heading: Use authorized targets
sections.body: Only use diagnostic commands against localhost, explicitly created lab hosts, or a simulator network. Never scan external networks.

practice.prompt: A synthetic host has an up interface, a valid IP, and failed name resolution. Identify the next safe question and explain why.

quiz.question: Why should a classroom network diagnostic target a sandbox host?
options: It keeps testing authorized and isolated
It guarantees the network is healthy
quiz.answer: It keeps testing authorized and isolated

lab.objective: Inspect a synthetic network path and classify the most likely layer needing investigation.

futureCompetencyCandidates: identify a network fault from evidence
reflectionPrompt: Which clue would you check first when a service cannot be reached, and why?
